newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Hong Kong gold ends down on European sales.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong gold ends down on European sales.

text.p: Spot gold prices in Hong Kong were buffeted by Japanese buying and Australian producer selling before settling below New York's Wednesday close, gold dealers and traders said on Thursday.

A plunging dollar/yen in morning trade provided good arbitrage opportunities for Japanese traders who sold gold in yen on the Tokyo Commodity Exchange and bought spot gold in U.S. dollars, Hong Kong-based gold dealers said.
"There was major buying from the Japanese and that pushed the price up to $377.70/378.70 per ounce earlier this morning," said one gold trader at an international bank.
Bullion ended at US$377.50/378.00 an ounce on Thursday against New York's $377.70/378.20 close on Wednesday.
Some of the morning buying was countered by Australian producer sales, some gold dealers said.
Late Asian and early European trade saw heavy selling pressure on gold as bearishness in the silver market spilled over.
"If silver cannot hold at around $4.72/4.74 then gold will certainly dip," said a local gold trader, adding that general bearishness in the white metals was affecting gold.
"Things have been really busy today," said a gold trader, noting that if $377 did not hold then $375 was seen as the next level of resistence.
Local gold ended HK$7 lower at HK$3,481 a tael.
The carryover charge at the Chinese Gold and Silver Exchange Society was -4.50 on Thursday, up from its previous fix at -5.00.
